highlight.title: Generative AI and Firm Values
highlight.summary: Eisfeldt et al. construct the first workforce-level GenAI exposure measure and find an 'Artificial-Minus-Human' portfolio earned 5% in the two weeks following ChatGPT's release, directly linking labor exposure to GenAI to equity valuation signals.

highlight.title: Revelio Labs RPLS US Jobs Report: The US economy adds 56.9k jobs in September
highlight.summary: Revelio's RPLS tracker shows the US economy added only 56.9k jobs in September while active job postings fell another 1.8%, with the accompanying AI Labor Market Tracker documenting continued labor-market restructuring as GenAI adoption expands.

extractedStats.quote: Beneath that aggregate resilience, our latest AI Labor Market Tracker shows a continuously evolving labor market as adoption of GenAI tools expands.

highlight.title: Artificial intelligence technologies, skills demand and employment: Evidence from linked job ads
highlight.summary: Using establishment-level vacancy data from 2015–2022, Peede and Stops find AI-related job postings remain a low share overall but are associated with significant shifts in skill demand at the establishment level, with differential effects on employment growth by AI intensity.

highlight.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: September 2026 Jobs Report — Steadiness Without a Spark
highlight.summary: Indeed's Hiring Lab characterizes the September 2026 labor market as stable but lacking momentum, with job postings data suggesting hiring demand has plateaued as macroeconomic uncertainty persists.

highlight.title: Artificial intelligence and labor investment efficiency: evidence from U.S. firms
highlight.summary: Analyzing U.S.-listed firms from 2004–2020, Xing et al. find a positive and statistically significant association between AI adoption and labor investment efficiency, with mechanism analysis suggesting AI reduces over- and under-investment in labor headcount.

highlight.title: Robots and Women in Manufacturing
highlight.summary: Zuazu finds that industrial robot adoption reshapes gender composition in manufacturing employment, with the direction of the effect on women's employment share depending on baseline levels of female labor force participation across countries.

highlight.title: From Repetition to Maintenance: How Digital Transformation in Chinese Manufacturing Reshapes Workers' Skill Requirements
highlight.summary: Liu documents that digital transformation in Chinese manufacturing is systematically shifting demand away from repetitive-task workers toward maintenance and smart-manufacturing competencies, with educational requirements for factory positions rising measurably.

highlight.title: Enterprise AI at the Decision Point: A U.S.-Focused Systematic Review of Productivity, ROI, Workforce Change, and Governance
highlight.summary: Rah and Johnson's systematic review of U.S. enterprise AI deployments synthesizes evidence on productivity gains, ROI, and workforce headcount changes, providing a meta-level quantitative baseline for AI adoption outcomes across sectors.

highlight.title: When Do AI Gains Become Broadly Shareable? A Policy Threshold for AI-Driven Automation
highlight.summary: Nayebi extends a standard task-automation growth model with an AI capability parameter to identify the policy thresholds at which automation productivity gains become broadly distributed rather than captured by capital, offering quantitative boundary conditions for displacement predictions.

highlight.title: The Impact of Digital Technologies on Self-Employment Dynamics in Italy
highlight.summary: Caselli, Cristofoletti, and Fracazza use province-level panel data (2015–2019) to show that advanced automation and big data adoption causally reduced self-employment in Italian manufacturing macrosectors, with heterogeneous effects across skill levels.
